text:
pagerbot: PagerDuty alert triggered: `GPU-serving-high-queue` on pool `prod-gpu-eu` (severity: P1)

irene (oncall-sre): I'm on it. seeing sustained queue growth on the prod-gpu-eu queue, latency > 2s for infer calls and token backlog increasing.

sam (infra): Confirmed. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to add nodes — hitting cloud provider scale limit and rate limits. current pool size 48, requested 80, cloud quota 50.

mike (runtime): Curling runtime endpoints shows many pods returning 503s with driver errors. grabbing logs.

lisa (eng-sre): putting quick metrics:
- queue length: from 200 -> 1800 in 12m
- 5xx rate: 12%
- p95 latency: 2300ms
- tokens/sec throughput down 40%

mike (runtime): logs snippet from one GPU pod:```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] runtime: cuda error: Xid 79, GPU fault detected
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] driver: kernel oops, dumping stack
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] infer: process OOM in /dev/nvidia0, killed
```

irene (oncall-sre): that Xid 79 pattern matches previous node flaps we saw. suspect driver-runtime instability reducing effective capacity (pods restarting, GPUs going offline).

sam (infra): cloud quota is the blocker for autoscale. I can request a temporary bump but that's slow. quick mitigation: spin up a smaller pool in a different region (prod-gpu-us) and failover routing, or move some low-priority tenants to CPU fallback. thoughts?

emma (cs): we have two mid-enterprise customers showing elevated errors: AcmeCorp and BrightBank. both are ~12% of total qps combined. flagging for customer comms if we expect >30m.

mike (runtime): plan: 1) isolate flapping nodes (cordon+drain), 2) restart nvidia driver on affected nodes, 3) deploy a temporary config to reduce per-pod worker threads to avoid kernel OOM blast radius.

lisa (eng-sre): doing cordon on node-gpu-14 and node-gpu-22 now to stop new workloads landing.

ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-14` -> OK
ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-22` -> OK

sam (infra): initiated a cross-region pool spinup: creating `prod-gpu-us` nodes with smaller instance type (A10x -> A100-similar). provisioning 12 nodes.

mike (runtime): restarting nvidia module on node-gpu-14 -> attaching logs.```
Mar 15 09:18:21 node-gpu-14 kernel: nvidia: driver unloaded
Mar 15 09:18:22 node-gpu-14 runtime: restarting inference container...
Mar 15 09:18:27 node-gpu-14 runtime: health checks passing
```

irene (oncall-sre): after restart, node-gpu-14 remained stable for ~6m then another Xid 31 spike on node-gpu-22.

sam (infra): autoscaler still throttled because of cloud API rate limits; working with provider support to expedite. meanwhile I can increase replica counts for fallback CPU workers to absorb webhooks and non-latency-critical jobs.

emma (cs): will prepare a short customer note: "We're experiencing elevated inference errors in EU region due to GPU node instability; routing to alternate region and temporary CPU fallback to reduce errors. Next update in 30m."

lisa (eng-sre): implementing temporary routing rule: divert 20% of traffic to `prod-gpu-us` and 30% to CPU fallback pool for non-critical customers. applying canary.

ops-bot: Route change applied: 20% -> prod-gpu-us, 30% -> cpu-fallback (canary)

mike (runtime): noticed a kernel log pattern pointing to a specific driver revision: `nvidia-driver-525.85`. rolling back nodes to `nvidia-driver-520.61` on a small subset to test.

irene (oncall-sre): good call. which nodes?

mike (runtime): rolling to node-gpu-30 and node-gpu-31. execing:```bash
ssh node-gpu-30 'sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-520.61 && sudo modprobe nvidia'
```

sam (infra): cloud nodes up in US pool, but warmup time 6m. queue length peaked at 2100 but now trending down to 400 after route changes. 5xxs dropping to 4%.

lisa (eng-sre): tracking impact: AcmeCorp errors down from 18% -> 6% after diversion. BrightBank from 11% -> 5%. overall error budget recovering.

mike (runtime): rollback nodes back stable, Xid events not reproduced on rolled nodes so far. looks driver-related.

irene (oncall-sre): decision log: 1) keep diverted routing for 45m while we monitor; 2) continue rolling driver back across suspect nodes; 3) request quota bump and escalate cloud rate limit with provider; 4) open postmortem and allocate runtime + infra owners.

emma (cs): sent interim notice to impacted customers.

sam (infra): provider support acknowledges the rate limit and has temporarily raised our API throughput by 2x; requesting formal quota bump.

irene (oncall-sre): current status: queue length 180, p95 420ms, 5xx 1.8%, tokens/sec recovered to 92% of baseline. marking incident as "mitigated" but still under active monitoring. will hand off to oncall rotation for follow-ups.

lisa (eng-sre): creating incident ticket and linking runbook entries for driver rollbacks and autoscaler limits.

mike (runtime): follow up actions: gather 1h of kernel and driver logs, correlate Xid types, prepare candidate emergency driver pin for the next DC-wide rollout freeze.

irene (oncall-sre): assigning owners: runtime -> mike, infra -> sam, cs comms -> emma, postmortem -> lisa. I'll file the postmortem and schedule a 1p blameless review.

pagerbot: Incident resolved -> Status changed to MITIGATED by irene

irene (oncall-sre): closing thread. if anyone sees new flapping please reopen and ping pager. thanks all for fast coordination :thumbsup:
